newsitem.title: ISRAEL: West Bank landmine kills two Arab youths -officials.
newsitem.headline: West Bank landmine kills two Arab youths -officials.

text.p: Two 13-year-old Palestinian boys were killed on Thursday by a landmine explosion in the West Bank, PLO security officials said.
The officials had said earlier three youths were killed in the village of Anza, near the self-ruled town of Jenin, but revised the figure after further investigation.
They said Mohammad a-Barahmah and Nimr Jarrar found a landmine while playing near the village cemetery. It exploded as they were handling it.
Two other boys were wounded in the blast, the officials said.
It was unclear how long the mine had been there. The West Bank was last a battlefield between two armies in the 1967 Middle East war, when Israel captured the region from Jordan.
Anza is located in a part of the West Bank where Israel maintains overall security control under its peace deals with the PLO, but Palestinian police are also deployed.
In a statement, the Israeli army said it could confirm two deaths.

"An initial investigation this afternoon revealed that two Palestinians were killed by a bomb in Anza village in the Jenin area. The blast was extensive," the statement said. "Security forces are checking the cause of the incident."
On Saturday, an Islamic militant was killed in the same area of the West Bank when explosives he was handling detonated, PLO officials said.

Israeli security forces have been on high alert for weeks, fearing attempts by the Islamic Jihad guerrilla group to avenge the killing of its leader Fathi Shqaqi in Malta on October 26, 1995. Palestinians believe Israel carried out the assassination.
